It is stated that the said award is not acceptable and the Award amount has been received under protest and without prejudice to their rights.

The said land is surrounded by the well developed areas having all basic modern facilities i.e. well connected roads, adequate transport facility, hospitals, schools, colleges, reputed clubs, farmhouses, party lawns and banquet Halls and the said land is, therefore, having the market value @ Rs. 8000 per square yards, and furthermore,

It is also submitted that ld. LAC failed to appreciate that it is the distance and the potentiality of the land and not the village, which is to be kept in mind while awarding the compensation.
It is stated that the ld. LAC failed to take note of the judicial pronouncements and the government policy of 10% yearly escalation in the market value of the said land.

10. It is stated that the respondent no.2 has allotted the adjoining land to persons for residential as well as commercial purposes for more than Rs. 6000 per square yards and that too only to those who has applied for the plots/flats and shops well in advance, which shows that the land for residential and commercial purposes was not so easily available @ Rs. 6000 per square yards.

The respondent no.2 has been allotting the plots at the remotest and undeveloped land, therefore, it is clear that the respondent no.2 cannot gain/earn profit at the cost of causing loss to the petitioners.

The petitioner also claims lumpsum amount of Rs. 1 lakh per acre along with interest for loss of income.
The petitioners have also sought Rs. 5 lakhs on account of loss of avocation in as much as petitioners are lacking technical know how and have been left with no avocation to pursue.

sentences.text: Various factors were taken into account by the learned LAC while assessing the market value of the said land and, now the petitioners are claiming excessive and exorbitant enhancement of the land and structures.

The Delhi Land Reforms Act is applicable to the said land and the petitioners are not entitled for compensation in respect of any construction or structure which is raised without the sanctioning of law.
It is also submitted that the said land is not surrounded by any developed or undeveloped economies and can only be used for agricultural purposes.
The petitioners have not filed any documentary evidence to support their claims.
The learned LAC has categorised the said land into three categories on the basis of survey carried out as per the fertility and user of land.
The learned LAC in order to assess the market value adopted the indicative price fixed by government of NCT of Delhi for agricultural land and Delhi.

It is submitted that the learned LAC has rightly assessed the market value of the said land keeping in view all the aspects as provided under Section 23 and 24 of the Act and, has assessed the market value after considering the level of development, locality and situation of the area where the said land is situated.

It is submitted that the reference petition is misconceived and is liable to be dismissed as no ground or reason has been shown by the petitioners for enhancement in the market value of the land or superstructures which were correctly assessed by the learned LAC.

The area of the land and other amenities/facilities were also taken into consideration while assessing the compensation.

15. It is submitted that the compensation awarded by ld. LAC is adequate, sufficient just and legal and is based on cogent and reliable evidence, therefore, there is no scope for enhancement of the compensation amount.
The present reference petition is also barred by limitation.

The copy of the reference petition has not been forwarded to DDA, though the DDA is a beneficiary party, therefore,
DDA is not liable to pay any interest on the delayed period.

It is submitted that as per the directions of Land and Building Department, after announcement of the Award reference should be forwarded by LAC within 60 days from the date of filing of the reference.
The present petition has not been forwarded to the court within 60 days
therefore, DDA/beneficiary of land is not liable to pay interest thereupon.
The petitioner is also not admitted to be the owner/Bhumidhar with respect to the said land and has no locus standi to file the present petition for enhancement of compensation.

17. On the basis of pleadings of the parties and documents filed on record, the following issues were framed by the court on 30.09.2013 :  ISSUES.
1.

Whether the petitioner is entitled to enhancement in compensation, if so, to what amount ? OPP 2. Relief.

Counsel for the respondents have submitted that they both are relying upon the upon the evidence led by them in case bearing LAC no. 390 of 2016 titled as Mukhtyar Singh v. Union of India, Village Rani Khera.

sentences.text: I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have perused the entire record including the documents and the evidence led by the parties.
I have given a thoughtful consideration to the same.
My issue wise findings and determination are as under:  WHETHER THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED TO ENHANCEMENT IN COMPENSATION, IF SO, TO WHAT AMOUNT ? OPP 21.
The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioner.
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the acquired land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioners.

The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
22.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: To prove their case, the petitioners, through his counsel has adopted the evidence led in case Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 06.01.2023 and Ld.
Counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioner may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioner in the aforementioned case.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.
24.

Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Rani Khera covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioners is concerned.

25. In the Mukhtyar Singh (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Rani Kera acquired through Award No.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 as Rs. 19,73,583/ per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,73,583/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre.
26. The petitioners have not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the LAC no. 176 / 2016 (Award No. 08/2005 06/DC(NW)) Mehar Lal & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 13 of 14 petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.

entities.text: Mehar Lal & Ors. v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioner.
RELIEF 27.

In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs:
(i) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,73,583/ per acre.
An of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre is accordingly accorded.

(ii) Additional amount @ 12% (in terms of Section 23(1A) of the Act).
(iii)Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation ( in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
(iv)Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
28.
Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
Decree sheet be drawn accordingly.
File be consigned to record room after due compliance.
